title: Straining to urinate (especially a male cat)
signs: Repeated trips to the litter tray with little or no urine, crying, licking the genitals, hiding.
action: Emergency: see a vet immediately. A blocked urethra can be fatal within 24–48 hours.

title: Not eating for more than 24 hours
signs: Refuses all food. Kittens and overweight cats are at higher risk.
action: Call your vet the same day. Prolonged fasting can cause hepatic lipidosis (fatty liver).

title: Open-mouth or laboured breathing
signs: Panting at rest, open mouth, belly heaving, blue or pale gums.
action: Emergency: keep the cat calm and go to a vet or emergency clinic now.

title: Lily exposure
signs: Any contact with true lilies or daylilies (leaves, petals, pollen, vase water) even without symptoms yet.
action: Emergency: go to a vet immediately. Lilies cause acute kidney failure in cats; early treatment matters.
source: Cornell Feline Health Center; RSPCA Australia

title: Dog flea or tick product containing permethrin
signs: Tremors, twitching, drooling, seizures after contact with a treated dog or product.
action: Emergency: contact a vet or the Animal Poisons Helpline now. Never use dog spot-ons on cats.

title: Paralysis tick signs (east coast)
signs: Wobbly back legs, vomiting, change in voice, laboured breathing, found a tick.
action: Emergency: see a vet at once, even if you cannot find the tick.

title: Swallowed a human medicine or toxin
signs: Paracetamol, ibuprofen, antifreeze, rat bait, or chewed unknown plants.
action: Emergency: call a vet or the Animal Poisons Helpline immediately. Do not induce vomiting unless a vet tells you to.

title: Sudden hind-leg weakness or pain
signs: Dragging back legs, crying out, cold paws. Can be a blood clot linked to heart disease.
